name: Scotch Game
description: An active opening that opens the center early and develops pieces quickly.

variations.name: Schmidt Variation
variations.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. d4 exd4 4. Nxd4 Nf6 5. Nxc6 bxc6 6. Bd3 d5 7. exd5 cxd5 8. O-O Be7 9. c4 O-O 10. Nc3 Bb7

explanations.e4: Control the center and open lines for development.
explanations.Nf3: Develop your knight and attack the e5 pawn.
explanations.d4: Open the center with the defining Scotch pawn break.
explanations.Nxd4: Recapture with your knight and centralize it.
explanations.Nf6: Black develops and attacks your e4 pawn.
explanations.Nxc6: Exchange your knight for Black's c6 knight.
explanations.bxc6: Black recaptures with the b-pawn, accepting doubled c-pawns.
explanations.Bd3: Develop your bishop toward the kingside.
explanations.Be7: Black develops the bishop and prepares to castle.
explanations.Bb7: Black develops the bishop along the long diagonal.

variations.name: Classical Variation
variations.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. d4 exd4 4. Nxd4 Bc5 5. Be3 Qf6 6. c3 Nge7 7. Bc4 Ne5 8. Be2 Qg6

explanations.Nf3: Develop your knight and attack e5.
explanations.Nc6: Black develops and defends the e5 pawn.
explanations.Bc5: Black develops the bishop and pressures your knight on d4.
explanations.Be3: Defend your knight and challenge the bishop.
explanations.Qf6: Black develops the queen actively and creates pressure.
explanations.c3: Support the center and prepare to develop.
explanations.Nge7: Black develops the other knight toward the center.
explanations.Bc4: Develop your bishop toward the kingside.
explanations.Be2: Retreat the bishop to a flexible defensive square.
explanations.Qg6: Black places the queen actively on the kingside.

variations.name: Mieses Variation
variations.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. d4 exd4 4. Nxd4 Nf6 5. Nxc6 bxc6 6. e5 Qe7 7. Qe2 Nd5 8. c4 Ba6 9. b3

explanations.d4: Open the center with the Scotch pawn break.
explanations.Nxc6: Exchange your knight for Black's knight.
explanations.bxc6: Black recaptures and accepts doubled c-pawns.
explanations.e5: Gain space and attack the knight on f6.
explanations.Qe7: Black pins the advanced pawn against your king.
explanations.Qe2: Break the pin and support your e5 pawn.
explanations.Nd5: Black moves the knight to a strong central square.
explanations.c4: Challenge the knight and gain more space.
explanations.Ba6: Black develops the bishop and pressures c4.
explanations.b3: Support c4 and prepare to maintain your central space.
